question.text: Suresh wants to update his address, change his bank account, add a nominee, and request a CAS — all in one visit to the ISC. How should the RTA process these requests?

answer.text: Only two changes can be processed per visit; the rest must wait
Each request is processed separately with its own documentation requirements and verification process
All requests are processed through a single combined form
Address and bank change need AMC approval; nominee and CAS can be processed by RTA

explanation.text: The Logic: Each service request has its own documentation and verification workflow. Address change typically flows through KRA/KYC update or acceptable address proof. A bank mandate change requires bank account proof, with both old and new bank details supported where applicable. Nominee registration uses the current nomination form with the prescribed authentication such as eSign/two-factor confirmation. A CAS request can be processed as an immediate service. All can be initiated in the same visit, but each follows its own timeline and compliance checks. The Trap: There is no fixed limit on the number of requests per visit, and they cannot be combined into a single form because each has distinct documentation requirements. The RTA processes them independently rather than as a bundle. Note: Some changes (address, bank, contact) involve KYC/cooling-off treatment, while nominee registration uses its own current authentication flow. Asking the investor to bring the right proof up front avoids return visits.
